attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, endorsed in his own voice.

semantics.note: The drafter keeps the counterfactual price comparison and the firm 'far broader adoption' and 'far less controversy' wording. It is a present-tense comparative observation with no hedge.

contract.note: The contract reads the purchase as a valuation comparison, which is fair. But 'not that much more', the adoption segment and the measure of controversy are undefined, so the result depends on readings the speaker did not supply. The contract rightly refuses to rest on one unstated segment.

evidence.note: CNBC, 7 Jan 2026: Anthropic term sheet at $350B. This is a fundraising valuation, not a merger price. It is a valuation input but does not settle whether the premium is modest.
Reuters: xAI valued at $250B in the 2 Feb merger. Against e1 that is a 40% premium on a different transaction basis. The arithmetic does not settle the qualitative 'not that much more'.

Menlo, Dec 2025: Anthropic has 40% of enterprise LLM API share. It covers an earlier period and one market segment, and Menlo is an Anthropic investor. It does not establish broader adoption across all segments.
EC opened a DSA probe into Grok on X on 26 Jan 2026 over sexualised imagery. This shows a serious xAI-related controversy but offers no consistent comparison with Anthropic.
AAP FAQ, Sept 2025: Anthropic's $1.5B settlement over pirated books. A material Anthropic controversy, but an isolated example, not a comparative measure.

reviews.rationale: Anthropic's $350B valuation is 40% above xAI's $250B, and nothing fixes whether that counts as 'not that much more'. The adoption evidence is enterprise-only and predates the window. The controversy items are isolated examples, not a consistent comparison. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met, so the packet does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, endorsed in his own voice.

semantics.note: The user-count clause is firm. The prestige clause keeps its 'seems to be' hedge. concerns_providers lists only OpenAI and omits xAI and Google, a minor tagging gap.

contract.note: Reading 'doesn't have the users' as fewer active users than ChatGPT in January 2026 is an ordinary, fair plain reading. Leaving the hedged prestige clause unscored follows policy.

evidence.note: Apptopia brief, published 3 Feb 2026: ChatGPT held 45.3% of the chatbot-app market in January 2026. The measure covers apps only.
Same Apptopia brief: Grok's DAU share peaked at 15.2% in January 2026, well below ChatGPT under the same methodology and period.

reviews.rationale: In Apptopia's January 2026 chatbot-app data, ChatGPT had about 45% of the market against about 15% for Grok, from one provider, period and method. The data covers apps only, not web or in-X use, but the gap is wide and the packet holds no contrary measurement. The firm audience clause is supported. The hedged prestige clause is not scored.
